High Court Of Madhya Pradesh

sentences.text: Shri Mithilesh Prasad Tripathi - Advocate for appellant  Shri Akhilendra Singh - Govt. Advocate for respondent/S Heard on I.A. No.7713/2022 which is first application under Section 389 of Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 filed on behalf of the appellant - Sanju @ Sanjay for grant of bail and suspension of remaining jail sentence.

02. Appellant has been convicted vide judgment dated 18.04.2022 passed by the learned Special Judge (POCSO Act), District Burhanpur in S.C. No.04/2020 for offence punishable under Section 366 of the Indian Penal Code and sentenced to undergo RI for 5 years with fine of Rs.5,000/-,
Section 363 of IPC, Section 5(l) r/w 6 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 and sentenced to undergo RI for 20 years with fine of Rs.15,000/- and Section 376(2)(N) of IPC,
with default stipulations.
03.

entities.text: Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the appellant submits that appellant is innocent and has been falsely implicated in the case.
Prosecutrix remained with the appellant for seven months and there is two months delay in lodging the report of missing person.
Mother of the proscutrix has turned hostile.
Prosecutrix has not made any specific allegations about force used upon her.
Age of prosecutrix has not been proved by cogent evidence like date of birth and school record.
Appellant was aged about 21 years with no criminal record and he has completed incarceration in jail for almost four 2 CRA-4119-2022 years.

Hence, in such circumstances, prayer is made for suspension of the jail sentence and grant of bail.
04.
Learned counsel for the respondent / State opposes the application and prays for its rejection.

05. Considering the facts and circumstances of the case and arguments advanced by learned counsel for the parties, without commenting on the merits of the case, this Court is of the considered opinion that the application for suspension of custodial sentence filed on behalf of the appellant deserves to be allowed.

sentences.text: 1 06. Accordingly, I.A. No.7713/2024 is allowed and the execution of remaining jail sentence of the appellant is hereby suspended till the final disposal of this appeal.

It is directed that appellant - Sanju @ Sanjay be released on bail subject to depositing the fine amount, if not already deposited and upon furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand Only) with one solvent surety of the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court, with a further direction to appear before the Registry of this Court on 05.05.2025 and on such other dates, as may be fixed by the Registry of this Court in this regard during the pendency of this appeal.
List for final hearing in due course.
Certified copy, as per rules.
